# 1 Samuel Chapter 28 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 166v–167r | **Source Image:** 1SA_028_page_001.jpg, 1SA_028_page_002.jpg

---

**1** In those days the Philistines mustered their forces to fight Israel. Achish told David, "You understand, of course, that you and your men must march with me in the army."

**2** David said, "Then you will see for yourself what your servant can do." Achish replied, "Very well — I'll make you my permanent bodyguard."

**3** Now Samuel was dead. All Israel had mourned for him and buried him in his hometown of Ramah. Saul had banished all mediums and spiritists from the land.

**4** The Philistines assembled and camped at Shunem, while Saul gathered all Israel and camped at Gilboa.

**5** When Saul saw the Philistine army, terror gripped him and his heart pounded.

**6** He inquired of the LORD, but the LORD did not answer him — not through dreams, not through the Urim, not through prophets.

**7** Then Saul told his officials, "Find me a woman who is a medium, so I can go and consult her." His officials said, "There is one at En-dor."

**8** So Saul disguised himself, put on different clothes, and went to the woman at night with two of his men. He said, "Consult a spirit for me. Bring up the person I name."

**9** But the woman said, "Surely you know what Saul has done — he has cut off the mediums and spiritists from the land. Why are you setting a trap for me to get me killed?"

**10** Saul swore to her by the LORD, "As surely as the LORD lives, you will not be punished for this."

**11** Then the woman asked, "Whom shall I bring up for you?" He said, "Bring up Samuel."

**12** When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed. She said to Saul, "Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!"

**13** The king said, "Don't be afraid. What do you see?" The woman said, "I see a spirit coming up out of the ground."

**14** "What does he look like?" Saul asked. "An old man wearing a robe is coming up," she said. Then Saul knew it was Samuel, and he bowed facedown to the ground.

**15** Samuel said to Saul, "Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?" Saul said, "I am in terrible trouble. The Philistines are attacking me, and God has turned away from me. He no longer answers me — not through prophets, not through dreams. So I have called on you to tell me what to do."

**16** Samuel said, "Why do you ask me, now that the LORD has turned away from you and become your enemy?

**17** The LORD has done exactly what He announced through me. He has torn the kingdom out of your hands and given it to your neighbor — to David.

**18** Because you did not obey the LORD and did not carry out His fierce anger against the Amalekites, the LORD has done this to you today.

**19** The LORD will hand over both Israel and you to the Philistines. Tomorrow you and your sons will be with me. The LORD will also hand Israel's army over to the Philistines."

**20** Immediately Saul collapsed full-length on the ground, paralyzed with fear at Samuel's words. His strength was gone — he had eaten nothing all day and all night.

**21** The woman came to Saul and saw how shattered he was. She said, "Look, your servant obeyed you. I risked my life to do what you asked.

**22** Now please listen to me — let me give you something to eat so you'll have the strength to go on your way."

**23** He refused. "I won't eat," he said. But his servants and the woman urged him, and finally he gave in. He got up from the ground and sat on the bed.

**24** The woman had a fattened calf at the house. She quickly slaughtered it, took some flour, kneaded it, and baked bread without yeast.

**25** She served the food to Saul and his men, and they ate. Then they got up and left that same night.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **28:6 — the silence of God**: Three channels of revelation — dreams, Urim, prophets — all return silence. This is the most terrifying verse in Saul's story. God has not merely turned away; He has gone completely silent.

2. **28:10 — "Saul swore by the LORD"**: The irony is staggering: Saul invokes the LORD's name to guarantee safety for a practice the LORD explicitly forbids. He uses God's authority to violate God's law.

3. **28:14 — the robe**: Samuel is recognized by his robe — the same robe whose corner Saul tore in chapter 15, when Samuel told him the kingdom was torn from him. Even in death, Samuel wears the garment that symbolizes Saul's rejection.

4. **28:19 — "with me"**: The most chilling sentence in the book. "Tomorrow you and your sons will be with me" — in the realm of the dead. This isn't comfort; it's a death sentence. And it includes Jonathan, who has done nothing wrong.

5. **28:21-25 — the last supper**: There is something deeply human about this ending. A condemned king, a terrified medium, and a final meal before the battle that will end everything. The woman's compassion is the only warmth in the chapter.

— PNEUMA
